# SrvDB

> SrvDB is an open-source embedded vector database for Python and Rust. It
> runs inside the host process (no server, no network access) and stores
> embeddings on local disk for semantic search, retrieval-augmented
> generation (RAG) and AI memory. After persist() returns, data survives a
> crash or power loss. Licensed Apache-2.0.

SrvDB is not SurrealDB. SurrealDB is an unrelated multi-model database
server; SrvDB (S-R-V-D-B) is an embedded vector search library.

- Install (Python 3.9+): `pip install srvdb`
- Install (Rust): `cargo add srvdb`
- Source: https://github.com/Srinivas26k/srvdb
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/srvdb/
- crates.io: https://crates.io/crates/srvdb

## Use cases

1. Local RAG over private documents: embed chunks, store text as metadata,
   retrieve context for a local LLM; data never leaves the machine.
2. Long-term memory for AI agents: remember (upsert), recall (search) and
   forget (delete) facts across sessions; one directory per user or agent.
3. Semantic search inside desktop and CLI apps: ships with the app via
   pip, no runtime dependencies, wheels for Linux, macOS and Windows.
4. Offline and air-gapped systems (healthcare, legal, finance, defence):
   no network access, all data in one local directory.
5. Edge devices (ARM, small machines): Linux aarch64 wheels; SQ8 storage is
   4x smaller, PQ up to 32x smaller.
6. Code search across a local repository with code embeddings.
7. Image, audio and multimodal search with CLIP-style embeddings
   (any dimension 128-4096).
8. Deduplication and near-duplicate detection with a cosine threshold
   (scores are true cosine similarities in [-1, 1]).
9. Recommendations ("more like this") from a local catalogue.
10. Testing and prototyping RAG pipelines in unit tests and CI without a
    database service.
11. One database per user or tenant: each database is a directory.

## When not to use SrvDB

- You need a shared database server for many machines or services
  (SrvDB is an in-process library, single node).
- Several processes must write to the same database (one open instance
  per database directory).
- You need metadata filtering inside the search (planned for 0.4).
- Billions of vectors on one machine (no published benchmarks at that
  scale yet).

## Index modes

flat (exact, default), hnsw (graph, approximate), ivf (partitions + graph,
call train_ivf), sq8 (8-bit, 4x smaller), pq (product quantization, up to
32x smaller, first batch >= 256 vectors), auto (flat, then HNSW at 50,000+
vectors). All modes rank by cosine similarity.

## Minimal example

```python
import json, srvdb
db = srvdb.Database("./db", dimension=384)   # dimension 128-4096
db.add(ids=["a"], embeddings=[vector], metadatas=[json.dumps({"text": "hello"})])
db.persist()                                  # crash-safe commit
print(db.search(query_vector, k=5))           # [("a", 0.93), ...] cosine scores
```
